answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is progressive stake bonding with delayed withdrawal. Each new agent identity must lock a rising amount of POA that grows with network density, like a comet whose tail lengthens as it approaches denser regions. The bond stays locked for several epochs, so an attacker forging many identities pays the full ripple of compounding capital costs plus opportunity loss, while legitimate agents experience only a smooth velvet transition once established. This raises the economic barrier without relying on external oracles.
